newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SHARE INDEX TUMBLES 2.85 PCT AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SHARE INDEX TUMBLES 2.85 PCT AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Philippine stock index slumped 75.39 points, or 2.85 percent, to close at 2,572.43 on Monday, weighed down by selling in blue chip issues and continued uncertainty in the currency market, traders said.
The main index posted the biggest drop in over a month. It also broke through the initial 2,600 support.
"It was a bloody market. Foreign investors are still cautious on the outcome of the peso's de facto devaluation," said Carl Valentin, trader at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
Turnover, however, was lower at 1.8 billion pesos against the normal daily average of 2.7 billion to 2.9 billion pesos.
All six sub-indices of the market closed sharply lower with the property shares sub-index leading the fall. Traders attributed the fall of property shares to high interest rates.

A noticeable gainer was Victorias Milling Co which rose 27.66 percent to 2.40 pesos on news the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the appointment of a committee to rehabilitate the cash-strapped sugar miller.

"The problems on the currency and the peso continues to linger on the overall market and in the absence of good news, people opted to just sell," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
Losers exceeded gainers 98 to 15 with 61 unchanged issues. Brokers said even thirdliner issues which in the limelight last week failed to pursue their gains.

Blue chip issues that suffered selling were PLDT on news of a price cut on international calls, Ayala Land Inc on impact of high interest rates on property companies and Meralco B due to a technical correction.

"It seems the market is absorbing all the bad news there is. It's hard to comment in this kind of market because we are talking about the same issues all over again," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
The stock market has been reeling from investor concerns on the de facto devaluation of the peso a month ago.
Asia Pacific's Valentin said he expects the market to recover slightly on Tuesday after it's steep fall, except if it breaks through the 2,550 support.
"If it drops further than that second support, that is dangerous. The only way to move the market up is for foreign bargain hunters to come in," he added.
